frame_quality — ASTROSTACK quality op

• Data kinds: image2d → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.frame_quality(image, threshold_sigma=5.0, max_stars=25, min_separation=3, psf_box=11, n_score_stars=5) (to call the implementation directly, import astrostack; astrostack.frame_quality(image, threshold_sigma=5.0, max_stars=25, min_separation=3, psf_box=11, n_score_stars=5); from the registry, opsastrostack.get("frame_quality"))

Usage

Score one frame — sharpness, FWHM, background, roundness, and a point for selection.

Historically, the selection criterion of lucky imaging is "the peak intensity of a reference star" (Law, Mackay & Baldwin, *Lucky imaging: high angular resolution imaging in the visible from the ground*, A&A 446, 739 (2006)) —— the better the atmosphere at a given moment, the more the same total flux gathers into fewer pixels, so peak / total flux rises. That is adopted here too, multiplied by roundness to reject tracking elongation::

score = median(roundness) * median(peak_fraction)

peak_fraction is, for the n_score_stars brightest stars, (peak pixel - background) / aperture flux. It is scale-independent (it does not move when exposure time or gain change), so it can be used as is for comparisons between frames.

sharpness is separately the classic focus measure: the variance of the Laplacian divided by the variance of the image (Pech-Pacheco et al., *Diatom autofocusing in brightfield microscopy*, ICPR 2000). It moves when the number of stars changes, so it is not used for selection, but it is kept because it is the only measure that yields a value even for a frame with no stars at all.

Returns dict (table vocabulary). Keys are n_stars / background / noise_sigma / fwhm_px (median FWHM of the detected stars) / roundness / peak_fraction / peak_snr / sharpness / score / total_flux. When there are no stars at all, the star-derived values are nan and score is 0.0 ("do not select" is the correct answer, so sorting is not broken by nan).

Raises ValueError: not 2-D / contains non-finite values / *n_score_stars* less than 1.
